decision_description: The budget gate validator accepted a demo placeholder budget response (budget_response_placeholder.json) as satisfying the Phase 7 gate conditions. The gate pass declaration was set to 'pass' on the basis of: (1) the received/ directory being non-empty with a structurally conformant budget response present; (2) the budget response conforming to interface_contract.json v1.0 (protocol: lump_sum_budget_planner_v1) with all required response-level fields present (response_id, schema_version, work_packages, partners); (3) all 9 WP IDs (WP1–WP9) from wp_structure.json being present in the budget response; (4) all 8 partner IDs (ATU, CERIA, BIIS, ISIA, NIHS, ELI, BAL, FIIT) being present in the budget response; and (5) no blocking inconsistencies with resolution=unresolved existing. The decision to treat structural conformance as sufficient for gate passage — without requiring expert-validated numeric budget values — was made explicitly, with the placeholder nature of all numeric figures recorded as a non-blocking finding (NBF-01) in the gate assessment artifact.
alternatives_considered: Declare gate_pass_declaration=fail on the grounds that the budget response contains only illustrative placeholder values and does not represent an expert-approved budget output from the external Lump Sum Budget Planner system. This alternative was rejected because the Phase 7 gate conditions as defined in CLAUDE.md §7 require structural conformance to the interface contract and WP/partner coverage — not validation of numeric budget value accuracy, which is outside the scope of the orchestration system's gate logic.

Defer gate evaluation pending receipt of a non-placeholder budget response. This alternative was rejected because the demo context explicitly establishes the placeholder as the operative budget response for this run, and the interface contract (lump_sum_budget_planner_v1 v1.0) does not include a field or rule requiring non-placeholder status as a gate condition.

Perform numeric value materialization and cross-check budget figures against effort estimates. This alternative was rejected as a constitutional violation: CLAUDE.md §7 Phase 7 constitutional constraint 1 prohibits materializing, storing, quoting, or writing numeric budget values from the external budget response into any Tier 4 artifact. Structural coverage check only was the constitutionally compliant approach.
tier_authority_applied: CLAUDE.md §7 — Phase 7 budget gate conditions: gate passes when (1) received/ directory is non-empty, (2) budget response conforms to interface_contract.json v1.0 (protocol: lump_sum_budget_planner_v1), and (3) no blocking inconsistencies with resolution=unresolved exist; and CLAUDE.md §7 Phase 7 constitutional constraint 1 prohibiting numeric budget value materialization
rationale: The Phase 7 gate is a structural conformance gate, not a financial accuracy gate. The governing authority (CLAUDE.md §7) defines gate passage in terms of: presence of a budget response in the received/ directory, conformance to the interface contract schema, and absence of unresolved blocking inconsistencies. All three conditions were satisfied by the placeholder budget response. The placeholder nature of numeric values is a known and disclosed limitation of the demo context, recorded transparently as NBF-01 in the gate assessment. The constitutional constraint prohibiting numeric value materialization was observed throughout: the gate assessment performed structural coverage checks only (wp_id and partner_id presence/absence; field type presence) without quoting or storing any cost or effort figures. The decision to pass the gate is therefore consistent with both the gate logic authority and the constitutional constraint.
